## 1. Goal

A preprint with a DOI describing the RECORD-1 three-lesion tumor model, written
from the 2011 ASCO poster (abstract 4602), with the five poster authors or
their stated consent.

Out of scope: refitting the model or any new analysis of RECORD-1 data. The
preprint reports what the 2011 analysis found. Section 5 records the decision
this rests on.

## 2. The Poster

Stein AM, Carter A, Hollaender N, Motzer R, Sarr C. Quantifying the effect of
everolimus on both tumor growth and new metastases in metastatic renal cell
carcinoma (RCC): a dynamic tumor model of the RECORD-1 phase III trial. J Clin
Oncol 29, 2011 (suppl; abstr 4602). ASCO Annual Meeting, Chicago, 3–7 June
2011. [PDF](https://github.com/iamstein/Publications/blob/main/Posters/Stein11_ASCOposter_RAD_3lesions.pdf).

Everything in this section was transcribed on 2026-10-13 from text extracted
from the PDF, whose multi-column layout scrambles the order. Each item is ⚠️
until checked against the poster image.

### 2.1 Data

RECORD-1 (NCT00410124) randomized patients with metastatic RCC who had
progressed on sunitinib or sorafenib to everolimus 10 mg daily or placebo.
Dose reduction to 5 mg daily was allowed for toxicity. The analysis used local
radiology for the 407 patients with a baseline tumor assessment: the sum of
longest target lesion diameters (SLD), nontarget lesion progression status,
and new lesion appearance.

### 2.2 Model

Target lesions follow, by nonlinear mixed effects,

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = (r - E_\text{dose})\,y
$$

where $y$ is SLD, $r$ the placebo growth rate and $E_\text{dose}$ the
dose-dependent everolimus effect. The extracted text reads `dy/dt = r – Edosey`,
so the bracketing is a guess to check against the image.

Nontarget and new lesions carry no measured size, so the model assumes each
grows by the same equation and maps the latent size to a probability of
progression.

- **Nontarget lesions.** With $\Delta y\%$ the percentage change from baseline,
  $$
  f(\Delta y\%) = \frac{(100\% + \Delta y\%)^8}{(150\%)^8 + (100\% + \Delta y\%)^8}
  $$
  A 50% increase gives a probability of 0.5 and a 100% increase gives 0.91.
- **New lesions.** With $y$ the longest diameter of the new lesion, starting
  undetectable at 0.1 cm,
  $$
  f(y) = \frac{y^3}{(0.5\ \text{cm})^3 + y^3}
  $$
  A lesion at the 0.5 cm imaging resolution is detected with probability 0.5,
  and one at 2 cm with probability 0.984.

The 5 mg and 10 mg effects were fitted as separate parameters for target
lesions. For nontarget and new lesions the data did not support two, and one
effect was shared. Correlating the placebo growth rates $r$ across the three
lesion types improved the fit (P < .001). The three lesion predictions were
combined by the RECIST rules into a predicted time to progression for each
patient.

### 2.3 Results

| Quantity | Placebo | 5 mg | 10 mg |
|---|---|---|---|
| Change in SLD after 1 year, average patient | +142.1% ± 98.3% | +22.4% ± 17.2% | −15.7% ± 11.5% |
| Nontarget progression after 1 year (90% CI) | 95.0% (81.8, 99.5) | 64.3% (33.2, 90.0), 5 and 10 mg pooled | |
| New lesion progression after 1 year (90% CI) | 90.1% (76.1, 96.8) | 52.6% (20.5, 82.4), 5 and 10 mg pooled | |

: Poster results, transcribed ⚠️ {tbl-colwidths="[40,20,20,20]"}

Both doses slowed all three lesion types against placebo (P < .0001), and
10 mg slowed target lesions more than 5 mg (P < .0001). Predicted
progression-free survival matched observed in both arms (Figure 4 of the
poster), with everolimus patients simulated on their actual dosing history,
placebo patients simulated without crossover, and deaths from causes other
than progression excluded.

## 3. Choice of Server

| Server | Takes this? | DOI | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| bioRxiv | ⚠️ Probably not | Yes | Directs clinical trial analyses to medRxiv |
| medRxiv | ⚠️ Probably | Yes | Screens submissions; asks for trial registration, ethics, funding and competing-interest statements, and an author declaration that all authors agree |
| Zenodo | ✅ Yes | Yes | No screening; posts anything, including the poster PDF itself |

: Candidate servers. The bioRxiv and medRxiv rows are from memory, not checked against either site's current policy {tbl-colwidths="[15,20,10,55]"}

Recommendation: medRxiv, with Zenodo as the fallback if medRxiv screening
turns it away on the grounds that it reports a 2011 analysis that cannot be
reproduced. Posting the poster PDF itself to Zenodo now is a separate,
cheaper step that gives it a DOI the day it is done, and does not preclude
either.

## 4. What the Manuscript Needs Beyond the Poster

1. Methods detailed enough to reimplement: the estimation software, the
   random effects and their covariance, the residual error models, how the
   nontarget and new lesion probabilities entered the likelihood, how the dose
   history entered $E_\text{dose}$, and parameter estimates with standard
   errors. None of these are on the poster. They exist only in the 2011
   analysis files, if anywhere.
2. A statement on the prior publications from the same analysis, Stein 2012
   and Stein 2013 (Section 6), saying what this one adds, and a related work
   section drawn from Sections 3, 4 and 9 of the
   [literature review](literature-review.qmd).
3. Author consent from all five, and Novartis clearance. RECORD-1 is a
   Novartis trial, and three authors were Novartis employees.
4. Trial registration, ethics and funding statements, carried over from the
   RECORD-1 primary publication.
5. A data availability statement. The individual data are Novartis's.

## 5. Decision: Write Up or Refit

| Option | Needs | Gives |
|---|---|---|
| A. Write up the 2011 analysis as it stands | The poster, and the 2011 analysis files for item 1 of Section 4 | A preprint in weeks |
| B. Refit on RECORD-1 data | Data access from Novartis, possibly through a data-sharing platform | A reproducible analysis, and months |

Recommendation: A. Option B is a new project, and nothing in Section 1
requires it. If the 2011 parameter estimates cannot be found, A shrinks to a
methods-and-figures note on Zenodo.

## 6. Open Questions

1. ✅ Answered 2026-10-13: the three-lesion model has not appeared in a full
   paper. Stein 2012 (*BMC Cancer* 12:311) publishes the target lesion model
   alone and cites the poster as its reference 22 for the nontarget and new
   lesion work. Stein 2013 (*Eur Urol* 64:994) is a Cox analysis of overall
   survival with no dynamic model. The [literature review](literature-review.qmd)
   found no later model that does what the poster does (its Section 9).
2. Where are the 2011 model files, the control stream and the parameter
   table?
3. Are the four co-authors reachable, and who at Novartis clears it?

## 7. Steps

1. ✅ Answer open question 1 (done 2026-10-13).
2. Post the poster PDF to Zenodo for a DOI.
3. Contact the co-authors and Novartis (open question 3).
4. Find the analysis files (open question 2).
5. Check every ⚠️ in Section 2 against the poster image.
6. Draft the manuscript from Sections 2 and 4.
7. Submit to medRxiv, or Zenodo per Section 3.
